title: U.S. House · California's 13th Congressional District
area: Central Valley, including Merced, Stockton, and Modesto-area communities in Merced, San Joaquin, and Stanislaus counties.

context.text: This district's boundaries changed under California Proposition 50, the mid-decade congressional redistricting measure voters approved in November 2025; Inside Elections' Nathaniel Rakich said the new map adds the city of Stockton to the district, pushing it from an evenly divided baseline to D+6, though Latino voters shifting right in recent years has made the district more competitive for Republicans. Incumbent Adam Gray and Republican Kevin Lincoln II advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary. In 2024, Gray defeated then-incumbent John Duarte (R) by 187 votes out of more than 210,000 cast; as of July 2026, major election forecasters rated the 2026 general election Lean Democratic or Tilt Democratic. As of June 30, 2026, Gray had raised $4.19 million and Lincoln had raised $2.24 million.

candidates.name: Adam Gray
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with about 42% of the vote.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for California's 13th Congressional District (since 2025)

summary.text: Adam Gray is the Democratic incumbent for California's 13th Congressional District, a Central Valley seat. Born and raised in Merced, he worked as a legislative aide and university lecturer, served in the California State Assembly from 2012 to 2022, and lost a 2022 House race before winning the seat in 2024 by 187 votes. His official biography says he is on the House Agriculture and Natural Resources Committees and is Whip of the Blue Dog Coalition.

background.text: Born in Merced, California, in 1977. His official biography says he was born and raised in Merced, where he lives.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of California at Santa Barbara.

Worked as a legislative aide with the California State Legislature and as an assistant lecturer with the University of California at Merced before his election to the Assembly. His official biography describes him as an educator at UC Merced.
Member of the California State Assembly from 2012 to 2022, representing Merced and Stanislaus Counties.

According to his official biography, he founded the California Problem Solvers Caucus in Sacramento and worked on establishing a medical school program at UC Merced, new water storage infrastructure and improved water access for Central Valley farmers.
Lost the November 2022 general election for California's 13th Congressional District to John Duarte, 50.2% to 49.8% (67,060 to 66,496 votes).
Defeated incumbent Rep. John Duarte in the November 2024 general election, 105,554 votes to 105,367, and took office on January 3, 2025.
Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture and the Committee on Natural Resources, and is Whip of the Blue Dog Coalition, according to his official biography.

priorities.text: Says he is focused on lowering the costs of food, housing, health care, and utilities for Central Valley families, citing bills he introduced to reverse Medicaid cuts and extend ACA premium tax credits.
Says water access is the number one issue he hears about in the district, and cites bills he introduced to expand water storage capacity and ease permitting for water infrastructure projects.
In a statement, said the Valley needs results rather than partisan politics and that he will work with either party to lower costs and strengthen farms and small businesses.
priorities.quote: The Valley doesn't need more politicians trying to score partisan points in Washington. We need results.

positions.summary: Introduced the Protecting Health Care and Lowering Costs Act of 2025 to reverse Medicaid cuts in the 2025 reconciliation law and permanently extend ACA enhanced premium tax credits.

Cosponsored the Stopping a Rogue President on Trade Act, which would limit the president's ability to unilaterally impose tariffs without congressional approval, and introduced the Stop Raising Prices on Food Act to protect farmers from tariff-related cost increases.

Says the border must be secured and federal agencies held to clear standards, while also cosponsoring the American Dream and Promise Act of 2025 to provide a citizenship pathway for Dreamers and voting against a DHS appropriations bill he said gave ICE and CBP a blank check without accountability reforms.

Says he strongly supports law enforcement and lists securing $1,031,000 for the Modesto Police Department's radio system and funding for a gang-violence task program during his time in the State Assembly.

His campaign site says he supported a War Powers Resolution to end U.S. military activity in Iran absent a declaration of war or authorization, and that Congress carries the responsibility to declare war.
positions.quote: Congress carries the solemn responsibility to declare war

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Agriculture, Subcommittee on Commodity Markets, Digital Assets and Rural Development, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
One of fourteen Democrats to help pass the Farm Bill in the House Agriculture Committee, and one of two Democrats to move the SPEED Act permitting bill out of the House Natural Resources Committee.
Introduced the End the California Water Crisis Package and the Central Valley Water Solution Act, bills that would authorize 21 additional water storage projects in California.

During his decade in the California State Assembly, secured $220 million to build a medical education building at UC Merced and $2 million for the Stanislaus County Office of Education to create the VOLT Institute job-training program in Modesto.

candidates.name: Kevin Lincoln II
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with about 28% of the vote. Previously ran for California's 9th District in 2024, losing to Josh Harder 51.8%-48.2%.

summary.text: Kevin Lincoln II is a Republican and U.S. Marine Corps veteran who describes himself as a security company executive and pastor. He was elected mayor of Stockton in 2020, serving from 2021 to 2024, and lost a 2024 race for California's 9th Congressional District. He is running on a platform that, per his campaign website, centers on the cost of groceries, gas and housing for Valley families.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Marine Corps; his campaign site notes he is a former member of the Marine Corps.
Earned an associate degree in business, a bachelor's degree in business management, and a master's degree in executive leadership.
Career experience includes working as a district manager with a private security company; Ballotpedia describes him as a security company executive and pastor.

Elected mayor of Stockton in November 2020, defeating incumbent Michael Tubbs 56.4% to 43.6% (57,276 to 44,206 votes); served from January 1, 2021, to December 31, 2024, and did not seek re-election in 2024.
Ran unsuccessfully for California's 9th Congressional District in 2024, losing to incumbent Josh Harder (D), 51.8% to 48.2%.
Advanced from the June 2, 2026, top-two primary in the 13th District after redistricting changed his district.

priorities.text: Campaign website said Washington's policies and partisanship are making life harder for the Valley and that leaders have done little to address the cost of groceries, gas, and housing.
priorities.quote: D.C. politicians have done little to address the cost of groceries, gas, and housing for Valley families. Now more than ever, we need a leader who will put people before politics.

priorities.text: Says that as mayor he balanced budgets without raising taxes and delivered an 18% pay raise and $42 million budget increase for police.
Supports the president's AI Action Plan, saying it prioritizes American innovation, national security, and domestic AI infrastructure.

positions.summary: Campaign site says that as mayor he "backed the blue," delivering an 18% pay raise and $42 million budget increase for police, and that in Congress he will fight what he calls soft-on-crime policies like early release and reduced sentences for repeat offenders.

record.text: Served as mayor of Stockton, California, from 2021 to 2024.
Ran for California's 9th Congressional District in 2024, losing to incumbent Josh Harder 51.8%-48.2%.
